title: [Audit] 🔐 Identity & Access
description: Who authenticated, how, from where, and what failed. Resolves the numeric user.name into real identities.

config.description: Distinct identities in all traffic, resolved as email, then API key name, then user.name — one per row of Identity first and last seen. The people among them, by email, are the Humans tile beside it. The line under the number counts the API keys among them that have no email, by name (a Cloud API key, which has none, by its id): a re-issued key keeps its name, so it counts once here and once per id in the API keys tile. A key named after a person (syn-new-hire-…) is still a key. The rest of the number is service accounts and built-in users (elastic/kibana, autoscaling), user names tried in a failed sign-in (admin, elastic), and the placeholders for requests that presented no identity (<anonymous>, <unauthenticated-…>) — each a row in that session.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | STATS BY attributes.user.email, attributes.api_key.name, attributes.user.name, attributes.user.domain | EVAL actor = COALESCE(attributes.user.email, attributes.api_key.name, attributes.user.name, "<anonymous>") | STATS `Identities` = COUNT_DISTINCT(actor), keys = COUNT_DISTINCT(actor) WHERE attributes.user.email IS NULL AND (attributes.api_key.name IS NOT NULL OR attributes.user.domain == "_cloud_api_key") | EVAL detail = CASE(keys == 0, "no API keys", keys == 1, "incl. 1 key name", CONCAT("incl. ", CASE(LENGTH(TO_STRING(keys)) <= 3, TO_STRING(keys), LENGTH(TO_STRING(keys)) <= 6, CONCAT(LEFT(TO_STRING(keys), LENGTH(TO_STRING(keys)) - 3), ",", RIGHT(TO_STRING(keys), 3)), LENGTH(TO_STRING(keys)) <= 9, CONCAT(LEFT(TO_STRING(keys), LENGTH(TO_STRING(keys)) - 6), ",", SUBSTRING(TO_STRING(keys), LENGTH(TO_STRING(keys)) - 5, 3), ",", RIGHT(TO_STRING(keys), 3)), CONCAT(LEFT(TO_STRING(keys), LENGTH(TO_STRING(keys)) - 9), ",", SUBSTRING(TO_STRING(keys), LENGTH(TO_STRING(keys)) - 8, 3), ",", SUBSTRING(TO_STRING(keys), LENGTH(TO_STRING(keys)) - 5, 3), ",", RIGHT(TO_STRING(keys), 3))), " key names")) | KEEP `Identities`, detail

config.description: Distinct email addresses in all traffic — the people Busiest human identities ranks. An Elasticsearch API key carries its creator's email, so a person can count here through a key they made without signing in; the line under the number says how many signed in through SAML SSO.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | STATS `Humans` = COUNT_DISTINCT(attributes.user.email), sso = COUNT_DISTINCT(attributes.user.email) WHERE attributes.user.domain == "cloud-saml-kibana" | EVAL detail = CASE(sso == 0, "none signed in by SSO", CONCAT(CASE(LENGTH(TO_STRING(sso)) <= 3, TO_STRING(sso), LENGTH(TO_STRING(sso)) <= 6, CONCAT(LEFT(TO_STRING(sso), LENGTH(TO_STRING(sso)) - 3), ",", RIGHT(TO_STRING(sso), 3)), LENGTH(TO_STRING(sso)) <= 9, CONCAT(LEFT(TO_STRING(sso), LENGTH(TO_STRING(sso)) - 6), ",", SUBSTRING(TO_STRING(sso), LENGTH(TO_STRING(sso)) - 5, 3), ",", RIGHT(TO_STRING(sso), 3)), CONCAT(LEFT(TO_STRING(sso), LENGTH(TO_STRING(sso)) - 9), ",", SUBSTRING(TO_STRING(sso), LENGTH(TO_STRING(sso)) - 8, 3), ",", SUBSTRING(TO_STRING(sso), LENGTH(TO_STRING(sso)) - 5, 3), ",", RIGHT(TO_STRING(sso), 3))), " signed in by SSO")) | KEEP `Humans`, detail

config.description: Distinct API keys seen in range, of both kinds: Elastic Cloud API keys (recorded by id only) and Elasticsearch (ES) API keys (by id and name); the line under the number splits them. One per row of API key inventory. A re-issued Elasticsearch key keeps its name under a new id and counts again.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE attributes.api_key.id IS NOT NULL OR attributes.user.domain == "_cloud_api_key" | STATS es = COUNT_DISTINCT(attributes.api_key.id), cloud = COUNT_DISTINCT(attributes.user.name) WHERE attributes.api_key.id IS NULL | EVAL `API keys` = es + cloud, detail = CASE(es + cloud == 0, "none in range", CONCAT(CASE(cloud == 0, "no Cloud", cloud == 1, "1 Cloud", CONCAT(CASE(LENGTH(TO_STRING(cloud)) <= 3, TO_STRING(cloud), LENGTH(TO_STRING(cloud)) <= 6, CONCAT(LEFT(TO_STRING(cloud), LENGTH(TO_STRING(cloud)) - 3), ",", RIGHT(TO_STRING(cloud), 3)), LENGTH(TO_STRING(cloud)) <= 9, CONCAT(LEFT(TO_STRING(cloud), LENGTH(TO_STRING(cloud)) - 6), ",", SUBSTRING(TO_STRING(cloud), LENGTH(TO_STRING(cloud)) - 5, 3), ",", RIGHT(TO_STRING(cloud), 3)), CONCAT(LEFT(TO_STRING(cloud), LENGTH(TO_STRING(cloud)) - 9), ",", SUBSTRING(TO_STRING(cloud), LENGTH(TO_STRING(cloud)) - 8, 3), ",", SUBSTRING(TO_STRING(cloud), LENGTH(TO_STRING(cloud)) - 5, 3), ",", RIGHT(TO_STRING(cloud), 3))), " Cloud")), " · ", CASE(es == 0, "no ES", es == 1, "1 ES", CONCAT(CASE(LENGTH(TO_STRING(es)) <= 3, TO_STRING(es), LENGTH(TO_STRING(es)) <= 6, CONCAT(LEFT(TO_STRING(es), LENGTH(TO_STRING(es)) - 3), ",", RIGHT(TO_STRING(es), 3)), LENGTH(TO_STRING(es)) <= 9, CONCAT(LEFT(TO_STRING(es), LENGTH(TO_STRING(es)) - 6), ",", SUBSTRING(TO_STRING(es), LENGTH(TO_STRING(es)) - 5, 3), ",", RIGHT(TO_STRING(es), 3)), CONCAT(LEFT(TO_STRING(es), LENGTH(TO_STRING(es)) - 9), ",", SUBSTRING(TO_STRING(es), LENGTH(TO_STRING(es)) - 8, 3), ",", SUBSTRING(TO_STRING(es), LENGTH(TO_STRING(es)) - 5, 3), ",", RIGHT(TO_STRING(es), 3))), " ES")))) | KEEP `API keys`, detail

config.description: Events authenticated through the cloud-saml-kibana SAML realm — a person in a browser. The line under the number counts Kibana user_login events: a session that began before the range shows events here but no new sign-in.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE attributes.user.domain == "cloud-saml-kibana" | STATS `SSO events` = COUNT(*), logins = COUNT(*) WHERE attributes.event.action == "user_login" | EVAL detail = CASE(logins == 0, "no new sign-ins", logins == 1, "1 new sign-in", CONCAT(CASE(LENGTH(TO_STRING(logins)) <= 3, TO_STRING(logins), LENGTH(TO_STRING(logins)) <= 6, CONCAT(LEFT(TO_STRING(logins), LENGTH(TO_STRING(logins)) - 3), ",", RIGHT(TO_STRING(logins), 3)), LENGTH(TO_STRING(logins)) <= 9, CONCAT(LEFT(TO_STRING(logins), LENGTH(TO_STRING(logins)) - 6), ",", SUBSTRING(TO_STRING(logins), LENGTH(TO_STRING(logins)) - 5, 3), ",", RIGHT(TO_STRING(logins), 3)), CONCAT(LEFT(TO_STRING(logins), LENGTH(TO_STRING(logins)) - 9), ",", SUBSTRING(TO_STRING(logins), LENGTH(TO_STRING(logins)) - 8, 3), ",", SUBSTRING(TO_STRING(logins), LENGTH(TO_STRING(logins)) - 5, 3), ",", RIGHT(TO_STRING(logins), 3))), " new sign-ins")) | KEEP `SSO events`, detail

config.description: Failed sign-ins (authentication_failed or anonymous_access_denied, one per request; the realm_authentication_failed events Elasticsearch writes for each realm an attempt tried are left out, so an attempt counts once) plus requests refused or failed after sign-in (access_denied and any other failed outcome). The line under the number counts the failed sign-in attempts (nobody signed in: these are not logins); the rest of the number is denied — refused or failed after sign-in. A denial is an authenticated identity hitting a permission wall, not someone guessing credentials. Same predicate as the two failure panels below.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE attributes.event.action IN ("authentication_failed","anonymous_access_denied") OR (attributes.event.outcome == "failure" AND (attributes.event.action IS NULL OR attributes.event.action != "realm_authentication_failed")) | STATS `Failed or denied` = COUNT(*), signin = COUNT(*) WHERE attributes.event.action IN ("authentication_failed","anonymous_access_denied") | EVAL detail = CASE(signin == 0, "no failed sign-ins", signin == 1, "1 failed sign-in", signin == `Failed or denied`, "all failed sign-ins", CONCAT(CASE(LENGTH(TO_STRING(signin)) <= 3, TO_STRING(signin), LENGTH(TO_STRING(signin)) <= 6, CONCAT(LEFT(TO_STRING(signin), LENGTH(TO_STRING(signin)) - 3), ",", RIGHT(TO_STRING(signin), 3)), LENGTH(TO_STRING(signin)) <= 9, CONCAT(LEFT(TO_STRING(signin), LENGTH(TO_STRING(signin)) - 6), ",", SUBSTRING(TO_STRING(signin), LENGTH(TO_STRING(signin)) - 5, 3), ",", RIGHT(TO_STRING(signin), 3)), CONCAT(LEFT(TO_STRING(signin), LENGTH(TO_STRING(signin)) - 9), ",", SUBSTRING(TO_STRING(signin), LENGTH(TO_STRING(signin)) - 8, 3), ",", SUBSTRING(TO_STRING(signin), LENGTH(TO_STRING(signin)) - 5, 3), ",", RIGHT(TO_STRING(signin), 3))), " failed sign-ins")) | KEEP `Failed or denied`, detail

config.description: Distinct Kibana browser sessions observed in range, and how many people (by email) they belong to.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE attributes.kibana.session.id IS NOT NULL | STATS `Kibana sessions` = COUNT_DISTINCT(attributes.kibana.session.id), people = COUNT_DISTINCT(attributes.user.email) | EVAL detail = CASE(`Kibana sessions` == 0, "none in range", CASE(people == 0, "no email recorded", people == 1, "1 person", CONCAT(CASE(LENGTH(TO_STRING(people)) <= 3, TO_STRING(people), LENGTH(TO_STRING(people)) <= 6, CONCAT(LEFT(TO_STRING(people), LENGTH(TO_STRING(people)) - 3), ",", RIGHT(TO_STRING(people), 3)), LENGTH(TO_STRING(people)) <= 9, CONCAT(LEFT(TO_STRING(people), LENGTH(TO_STRING(people)) - 6), ",", SUBSTRING(TO_STRING(people), LENGTH(TO_STRING(people)) - 5, 3), ",", RIGHT(TO_STRING(people), 3)), CONCAT(LEFT(TO_STRING(people), LENGTH(TO_STRING(people)) - 9), ",", SUBSTRING(TO_STRING(people), LENGTH(TO_STRING(people)) - 8, 3), ",", SUBSTRING(TO_STRING(people), LENGTH(TO_STRING(people)) - 5, 3), ",", RIGHT(TO_STRING(people), 3))), " people"))) | KEEP `Kibana sessions`, detail

config.title: Authentication method over time
config.description: Elasticsearch requests per interval by how they presented credentials: API key, token (SSO browser sessions and service accounts) or realm (username and password). One bar per credential type per interval, on a log scale, so a type carrying a fraction of a percent of the traffic is as readable as the bulk; an interval with no bar had no requests of that type. A shift in this mix is worth explaining.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE attributes.authentication.type IS NOT NULL | STATS events = COUNT(*) BY BUCKET(@timestamp, 75, ?_tstart, ?_tend), attributes.authentication.type | EVAL auth = CASE(attributes.authentication.type == "api_key", "API key", attributes.authentication.type == "token", "Token", attributes.authentication.type == "realm", "Realm", attributes.authentication.type == "saml", "SAML", attributes.authentication.type == "anonymous", "Anonymous", attributes.authentication.type == "internal", "Internal", attributes.authentication.type) | SORT auth

config.title: Credential type by identity
config.description: Which credential type each of the busiest identities presents, 12 at most; colour runs teal → blue → purple → pink as events grow (log scale; the legend is labelled at the smallest and largest cell and the decades between). Humans should authenticate by token (SSO); service identities by API key. Only Elasticsearch requests record a credential type, so identities seen only in Kibana or only anonymously are counted in Identities above but are not on this chart. A Cloud API key has no name and is shown as “_4KEO… · Cloud API key”, the first five characters of its id.

config.title: Events by identity origin
config.description: Events, not identities, by the email on the event: Elastic (@elastic.co), Tenant (any other address), or Machine (no email: service accounts, Cloud API keys, internal users and anonymous requests). Each origin's name carries its count, and the bars are on a log scale so a person's few dozen events are visible beside a key's hundreds of thousands: read the count, not the length. An origin with no bar had no events in range. One busy key can make Machine nearly all of the traffic while most identities are people. An Elasticsearch API key carries its creator's email, so traffic from a key a person created counts under that person's origin.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | STATS events = COUNT(*) BY attributes.user.email | EVAL actor_org = CASE(attributes.user.email IS NULL, "Machine", attributes.user.email LIKE "*@elastic.co", "Elastic", "Tenant") | STATS events = SUM(events) BY origin = actor_org | EVAL origin = CONCAT(origin, " · ", CASE(LENGTH(TO_STRING(events)) <= 3, TO_STRING(events), LENGTH(TO_STRING(events)) <= 6, CONCAT(LEFT(TO_STRING(events), LENGTH(TO_STRING(events)) - 3), ",", RIGHT(TO_STRING(events), 3)), LENGTH(TO_STRING(events)) <= 9, CONCAT(LEFT(TO_STRING(events), LENGTH(TO_STRING(events)) - 6), ",", SUBSTRING(TO_STRING(events), LENGTH(TO_STRING(events)) - 5, 3), ",", RIGHT(TO_STRING(events), 3)), CONCAT(LEFT(TO_STRING(events), LENGTH(TO_STRING(events)) - 9), ",", SUBSTRING(TO_STRING(events), LENGTH(TO_STRING(events)) - 8, 3), ",", SUBSTRING(TO_STRING(events), LENGTH(TO_STRING(events)) - 5, 3), ",", RIGHT(TO_STRING(events), 3)))) | SORT events DESC

config.title: Events by authentication realm
config.description: Events by the security realm that authenticated them. Each realm's name carries its count, and the bars are on a log scale so a small realm is visible beside the bulk: read the count, not the length. SAML SSO is interactive human sign-in (cloud-saml-kibana); Elasticsearch API key (_es_api_key) and Cloud API key (_cloud_api_key) are programmatic — an Elasticsearch key minted by a Cloud API key authenticates in the Cloud key's realm; Service account is Elastic's own components (_service_account). Any other realm is shown by its name. Anonymous and unauthenticated requests record no realm and are not counted, so the bars can sum to less than Events by identity origin beside it.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE attributes.user.domain IS NOT NULL | STATS events = COUNT(*) BY attributes.user.domain | EVAL realm = CASE(attributes.user.domain == "cloud-saml-kibana", "SAML SSO", attributes.user.domain == "_es_api_key", "Elasticsearch API key", attributes.user.domain == "_cloud_api_key", "Cloud API key", STARTS_WITH(attributes.user.domain, "_service_account"), "Service account", STARTS_WITH(attributes.user.domain, "_"), "Other internal", attributes.user.domain) | STATS events = SUM(events) BY realm | EVAL realm = CONCAT(realm, " · ", CASE(LENGTH(TO_STRING(events)) <= 3, TO_STRING(events), LENGTH(TO_STRING(events)) <= 6, CONCAT(LEFT(TO_STRING(events), LENGTH(TO_STRING(events)) - 3), ",", RIGHT(TO_STRING(events), 3)), LENGTH(TO_STRING(events)) <= 9, CONCAT(LEFT(TO_STRING(events), LENGTH(TO_STRING(events)) - 6), ",", SUBSTRING(TO_STRING(events), LENGTH(TO_STRING(events)) - 5, 3), ",", RIGHT(TO_STRING(events), 3)), CONCAT(LEFT(TO_STRING(events), LENGTH(TO_STRING(events)) - 9), ",", SUBSTRING(TO_STRING(events), LENGTH(TO_STRING(events)) - 8, 3), ",", SUBSTRING(TO_STRING(events), LENGTH(TO_STRING(events)) - 5, 3), ",", RIGHT(TO_STRING(events), 3)))) | SORT events DESC

config.title: Busiest API keys · top 10 at most
config.description: The busiest API keys of both kinds, one row per key, with request volume and how many distinct client IPs used it. Kind is Cloud (an Elastic Cloud API key: it has no name and is recorded by its id, so it reads “_4KEO… · Cloud API key”, the first five characters of the id in Key ID) or Elasticsearch (an Elasticsearch API key: id and name). A key used from many IPs is worth investigating. A re-issued key keeps its name under a new id, so a name can appear twice. The full list, with owner and first and last use, is API key inventory below. On a rolling time range each panel reads “now” at the moment it loads, and the newest events reach the stream a few seconds late, so a key still sending requests can show slightly different counts here and in the inventory, which loads a moment apart.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE attributes.api_key.id IS NOT NULL OR attributes.user.domain == "_cloud_api_key" | STATS events = COUNT(*), ips = COUNT_DISTINCT(client.ip) BY api_key = attributes.api_key.name, attributes.api_key.id, attributes.user.name | EVAL key_id = COALESCE(attributes.api_key.id, attributes.user.name), kind = CASE(attributes.api_key.id IS NULL, "Cloud", "Elasticsearch"), api_key = COALESCE(api_key, CASE((LENGTH(attributes.user.name) == 20 AND attributes.user.name RLIKE "[-_A-Za-z0-9]{20}" AND NOT attributes.user.name RLIKE "[0-9]{20}"), CONCAT(LEFT(attributes.user.name, 5), "… · Cloud API key"), "(no name)")) | SORT events DESC | LIMIT 10

config.title: Busiest human identities · top 10 at most
config.description: People by email, busiest first: the people the Humans tile counts, over all traffic, with the same event counts as Identity first and last seen, which also has when each was first and last seen and from how many IPs. The panel shows the top rows; the rest are in that session. Click an email to pin that person across the suite.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE attributes.user.email IS NOT NULL | STATS events = COUNT(*) BY attributes.user.email | SORT events DESC | LIMIT 10

config.title: Top failed or denied access · 10 at most (empty = good)
config.description: Failed sign-ins and refused requests grouped by identity, action and source IP, most frequent first; the top rows of what the Failed or denied tile counts. Result names the kind, as in the session below: failed sign-in (authentication_failed or anonymous_access_denied, one per request; the realm_authentication_failed events Elasticsearch writes for each realm an attempt tried are left out, so an attempt counts once), denied (access_denied: an authenticated identity refused an action), or failed (any other action, here because its outcome was failure). An Identity shown as “_4KEO… · Cloud API key” is an organization-level Elastic Cloud API key: the audit stream records it only by its opaque 20-character id, shown here by its first five characters; it has no name and no owner email. An empty panel means nothing matched in the time range, which is the healthy state; any row here is worth reading.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE attributes.event.action IN ("authentication_failed","anonymous_access_denied") OR (attributes.event.outcome == "failure" AND (attributes.event.action IS NULL OR attributes.event.action != "realm_authentication_failed")) | STATS events = COUNT(*), last_seen = MAX(@timestamp) BY attributes.user.email, attributes.api_key.name, attributes.user.name, action = attributes.event.action, ip = client.ip | EVAL actor = COALESCE(attributes.user.email, attributes.api_key.name, attributes.user.name, "<anonymous>") | STATS events = SUM(events), last_seen = MAX(last_seen) BY actor, action, ip | EVAL result = CASE(action IN ("authentication_failed","anonymous_access_denied"), "failed sign-in", action == "access_denied", "denied", "failed") | SORT events DESC | LIMIT 10 | EVAL actor = CASE((LENGTH(actor) == 20 AND actor RLIKE "[-_A-Za-z0-9]{20}" AND NOT actor RLIKE "[0-9]{20}"), CONCAT(LEFT(actor, 5), "… · Cloud API key"), actor)

config.title: Failed sign-ins and denied access · newest 1,000 at most (empty = good)
config.description: The newest failed sign-ins and refused requests, record by record. Discover stops at 1,000 rows, so on a busy range its result count is that cap and the Failed or denied tile is the total. Result names the kind: failed sign-in, denied (access_denied), or failed (any other failed outcome). Credential is the credential type, or the realm on a Kibana event, and reads “not authenticated” on a failed sign-in; Country reads “internal” for a private or carrier-NAT address, which is Kibana or the platform calling on someone's behalf. An Identity shown as “_4KEO… · Cloud API key” is an organization-level Elastic Cloud API key: the audit stream records it only by its opaque 20-character id, shown here by its first five characters; it has no name and no owner email. An empty panel means nothing matched in the time range, which is the healthy state; any row here is worth reading.

config.title: API key inventory
config.description: Every API key seen in range (up to 1,000), Cloud and Elasticsearch, busiest first — one row per key the API keys tile counts — with owner, volume, IP spread, indices touched and first and last use. Owner is the identity that created the key: a person's email, or, for a key minted programmatically, the Cloud API key that minted it, shown as “_4KEO… · Cloud API key” like that key's own row; a Cloud API key's own creator is not in the audit stream, so its Owner reads Cloud organization.

config.title: Identity first and last seen
config.description: Every identity in range (up to 1,000), all traffic — one row per identity the Identities tile counts — with its first and last appearance, Events (everything it did, the same count as Busiest human identities) and Signal events (what is left after the noise gate, the count the gated panels across the suite use). Newest first appearance on top. Widen the time range to tell a brand-new identity from one that was simply quiet. An Identity shown as “_4KEO… · Cloud API key” is an organization-level Elastic Cloud API key: the audit stream records it only by its opaque 20-character id, shown here by its first five characters; it has no name and no owner email.
